content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a soft-tissue mass.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

The tumor is the large bright heterogeneous mass occupying the posterior-lateral part of the limb. It spans roughly x 340–640 and y 270–600 in the left panel, which is x 1120–1420 in the right panel.

Candidate marks that fall inside the mass:
- 253 (1308, 365) lies in the anterior part of the mass.
- 251 (1289, 422) lies in the central part of the mass.
- 269 (1257, 460) lies near the center.
- 245 (1231, 422) is inside the mass.
- 234 (1206, 530) lies in the very bright area, and 205 (1244, 549) is nearby.
- 218 (1308, 537) is also inside.

The tumor center is roughly x 1260, y 440. Of the candidates, 269 (1257, 460) and 251 (1289, 422) are closest to that point. 269 sits in the mass between the very bright posterior component and the intermediate-signal region, and is the closest to the center overall.

ANSWER: 269
